summary: As of 2026-10-25, Docker Desktop 4.96.3 (2026-10-22) is still the newest GA and is newer than pin 4.86.0. Windows always-on stack should review before any upgrade: 4.96.3 continues the eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust (TLS intercept of Docker CLI/daemon; 4.96.1/4.96.2 said this is batched), plus remaining 4.96.2 Compose v5.6.1, 4.96.1 Engine 29.9.2, and 4.96.0 DHCP-on-LAN / 192.168.65.0/24 start hang / WSL mkfs-loop notes.
relevant_notes: 4.96.3 (2026-10-22) is still the newest GA as of this 2026-10-25 watch. Official docs HTML, docker/docs main (build_path /244472/), and a search of the same notes URL all lead with 4.96.3 — no 4.96.4 or 4.97.0. Newer than pin 4.86.0. Same-day patch after 4.96.2. Ships Docker Init v1.4.1, Docker Offload v0.7.19, Docker Model Runner v1.2.9, Docker Debug v0.49.0, Docker MCP v0.44.2, and kubectl v1.36.1. Init/Offload/Model Runner/Debug/kubectl are unused by this media/*arr + endurance-coach stack. Docker MCP here is Docker's MCP toolkit, not the endurance-coach mcp container — do not treat the v0.44.2 bump as a coach-mcp change. No Engine, containerd, Compose, or Buildx bump in 4.96.3 itself (those landed in 4.96.2 / 4.96.1 / 4.96.0). No Known issues section. No named CVE id in the 4.96.3 notes.

4.96.3 / 4.96.2 / 4.96.1 security: removed trust for certificates issued by the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA. An attacker with network access could intercept TLS connections made by non-browser clients such as the Docker CLI and daemon. Directly relevant to this always-on Windows stack (image pulls, Compose, registry/auth, ExpressVPN/LAN next to media/*arr and endurance-coach). Official Desktop notes do not assign a CVE id. Do not add third-party CVE numbers. Docker's security-announcements page also covers a Sandboxes-only CA refresh — this host's postgres/api/mcp and *arr containers are not Docker Sandboxes; do not treat sandbox recreate / sbx --pull always as a stack action.

4.96.1 / 4.96.2 IMPORTANT: the eMudhra CA distrust is rolling out in batches as individual Docker Desktop components are updated. Upcoming patch releases will cover remaining components; Docker recommends taking each patch as it becomes available. 4.96.3 is the next same-day batch (Init / Offload / Model Runner / Debug / MCP / kubectl) and repeats the CA security paragraph, but it does not repeat the 'upcoming patches' IMPORTANT callout. Do not assume the CLI/daemon CA work is finished from the 4.96.3 component list. Leave the pin at 4.86.0; a human should decide whether to take 4.96.3 now or wait for any remaining component patches.

4.96.3 all platforms: bundled-tool bumps only (Init, Offload, Model Runner, Debug, Docker MCP, kubectl). No Compose change (still v5.6.1 from 4.96.2), no Engine/containerd change (still Engine 29.9.2 / containerd v2.4.2). Compose v5.6.1 remains the relevant Compose delta for endurance-coach docker-compose.yml (postgres/api/mcp, restart: unless-stopped) and media/*arr Compose workloads.

Remaining 4.96.2 (2026-10-22): Compose v5.6.1 (from 4.95.0's v5.6.0). Also Docker Offload v0.7.6, Docker Agent v1.152.0, Docker Hardened Images CLI (dhictl) v0.0.9, Docker Desktop Build v0.39.1, and Docker Scout CLI v1.27.0 — Offload/Agent/dhictl/Build/Scout are not used by this media/*arr + endurance-coach stack. No Engine or containerd bump in 4.96.2 itself (those landed in 4.96.1 / 4.96.0). Same eMudhra CA security note as 4.96.3 (with the batched IMPORTANT callout that 4.96.3 omits). No Known issues section. No named CVE id. Directly relevant to endurance-coach docker-compose.yml (postgres/api/mcp, restart: unless-stopped) and media/*arr Compose workloads. Desktop notes do not list Compose bug-fix details.

Remaining 4.96.1 (2026-10-21): Engine 29.9.2 (from 4.96.0's v29.9.1), Buildx v0.38.1 (from v0.38.0), Credential helpers v0.9.12 (from 4.96.0's v0.9.10), Docker Offload v0.7.16. Same eMudhra CA security note as 4.96.2 (first batch of the CA distrust). No Known issues section. No named CVE id. Credential-helper bump matters if this host uses docker login / registry auth for image pulls.

Remaining 4.96.0 (2026-10-19): Engine v29.9.1 (from 4.94.0's v29.8.2), containerd v2.4.2 (from 4.94.0's v2.3.6), Buildx v0.38.0 (from 4.94.0's v0.37.2), and Credential helpers v0.9.10 (superseded by 4.96.1's v0.9.12). Compose was still v5.6.0 until 4.96.2. No Known issues section on 4.96.0. No named CVE id in the 4.96.0 notes.

4.96.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop's internal DHCP replies were sent onto the host's physical network. Networking-relevant on this always-on Windows host (ExpressVPN media stack + LAN access in configure_expressvpn_media_stack.ps1); leaked DHCP can confuse LAN/VPN routing next to media/*arr and endurance-coach published ports.

4.96.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop got stuck on 'Starting the Docker Engine...' when a Docker network took addresses inside Docker Desktop's internal network (192.168.65.0/24 by default). Overlapping networks are now rejected, and an existing one can be removed from the error dialog (desktop-feedback#659). endurance-coach compose has no custom subnet; check media/*arr Compose networks for 192.168.65.0/24 overlap before upgrade, or engine start / unless-stopped recovery can hang.

4.96.0 Windows: an unusable WSL data disk (for example already in use) repeatedly triggered failed mkfs format attempts instead of a clear error. Directly relevant to this always-on WSL host — a busy or locked engine disk could have been re-formatted (media/*arr volumes + endurance-coach postgres_data).

4.96.0 Windows: WSL distro startup failures showed a confusing 'bad magic string' error instead of the actual reason reported by wsl.exe. Improves WSL diagnosis for configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 / heal_full_stack.ps1.
4.96.0 Windows: full-disk errors during startup now show the disk-full recovery dialog instead of a generic failure. Useful on this media + coach host if the WSL/engine disk or host volume fills.
4.96.0 Windows: clearer error when Docker VMM cannot use the Windows hypervisor (for example some VMs where WSL 2 works). Relevant only if this host uses Docker VMM rather than WSL2.
4.96.0 all platforms: the error dialog could close unexpectedly on systems under memory pressure. Affects restart / recovery visibility on this always-on media + coach host after a RAM-tight reboot.

4.96.0 Mac-only: file ownership and transient 0:0 reporting on Apple Virtualization Framework + VirtioFS bind mounts (desktop-feedback#628/#649). Not a Windows VirtioFS fix; the Windows 4.90.0 bind-mount 0:0 note remains in-delta for ~/.garminconnect, ~/.endurance-coach, and media/*arr mounts.
4.96.0 all platforms: improved buffered filesystem performance and a FUSE fix that could expose stale bytes when extending files. Filesystem-adjacent; do not treat as a Windows VirtioFS claim.

4.96.0 all platforms: backend crashed and the engine became unreachable when a container's --volumes-from referred back to itself (desktop-feedback#286). endurance-coach and typical *arr Compose do not use that rename/volumes-from pattern.
Remaining 4.95.0 (2026-10-12): Compose v5.6.0 (from 4.91.0's v5.5.1). No Engine / containerd / Buildx bump in the 4.95.0 notes themselves. No Known issues section. No named CVE id.

4.95.0 Windows: the installer deleted the WSL data disk during an update when the data root was inside the Docker Desktop installation directory (desktop-feedback#667). Directly relevant to this always-on WSL host and scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 — a bad disk-image path can wipe the engine disk (media/*arr volumes + endurance-coach postgres_data) on upgrade.

4.95.0 all platforms: Settings accepted a disk image location inside the Docker Desktop installation directory, which the installer replaces on every update (same desktop-feedback#667). Confirm the WSL/Hyper-V disk image is not under Program Files\Docker before any upgrade.
4.95.0 Windows: updates could fail because app.asar was reported as locked by Docker Desktop. Directly relevant to winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop in update_docker_desktop.ps1.

4.95.0 Windows: Hyper-V VM could fail to start after a restart because its disk was still being compacted. Affects restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 if this host is on Hyper-V rather than WSL2.

4.95.0 Windows: Docker Desktop failed to start with the Hyper-V backend when the Windows hosts file was protected by an antivirus or endpoint security tool. Networking / name-resolution risk on a hardened always-on host.
4.95.0 Windows: dedicated error when the Hyper-V VM cannot start because the host does not have enough free memory. Useful on this always-on media + coach host if RAM is tight after a reboot.

4.95.0 Windows: WSL 3.0.1 reported docker info as 'Docker Desktop (containerized)' instead of 'Docker Desktop', which broke docker debug when Registry Access Management was enabled. WSL-relevant if this host has moved to WSL 3.0.1.

4.95.0 Windows: WSL/MSYS2 native symlink (LX symlink) handling, sparse stream exports via backup tar, and a named-pipe listener-close race were fixed. Applies to media/*arr and endurance-coach host bind mounts that use symlinks or WSL paths.

4.95.0 all platforms: Quit did nothing in the engine-failed error dialog, and that dialog took around 2 minutes to appear when the engine failed while starting. Gathering diagnostics from the same dialog failed repeatedly when Docker Desktop could not start. Affects restart / recovery visibility for post_boot_stack_recovery.ps1 and heal_full_stack.ps1.

4.95.0 Windows installer: intermittent MSI 1603 from analytics custom actions racing other installer steps; per-user install silently completed when Virtual Machine Platform was disabled (Desktop then could not start); per-user install from SYSTEM (SCCM/Intune) now fails with an explicit error instead of installing into the SYSTEM profile. This host's pin path is winget, not MSI/SCCM.
4.95.0 all platforms: engine restarted right after Docker Desktop started when an admin policy enabled Enhanced Container Isolation. Only relevant if this host is under a Docker org admin policy.

4.94.0 Windows: Docker Desktop service lost its automatic start mode after a WinGet or other external-installer update when the service had been installed with --always-run-service. Directly relevant to this always-on host and scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 (winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop).

4.94.0 Windows: fixed the 4.92.0 bug where WSL integration failed to start with 'timed out waiting for ... to be automounted' (desktop-feedback#695). This is the explicit fix for the 4.92.0 known issue (wsl.conf [automount] root=/ or a container bind-mounting a non-drive /mnt path such as /mnt/wslg). 4.93.0 already had a related WSL bind-mount proxy fatal-timeout fix; 4.94.0 names the automount-timeout failure directly.

4.94.0 all platforms: Resource Saver could pause the VM before the Docker API was ready, causing transient errors during engine startup or restart. Relevant to always-on restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 / Resource Saver wake (endurance-coach api/mcp use build: .).

4.94.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop service was left stopped after an update when it was running but not configured to auto-start. Always-on stacks that expect the engine to come back after an update can stay down until a human starts the service.

4.94.0 security: stored API keys were written in clear to Docker Desktop logs and included in diagnostics bundles. Logs also recorded unobfuscated values for IPC payloads that were JSON arrays or plain strings. Review diagnostics sharing if this host has been sending bundles.
4.94.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop could write a multi-gigabyte error file and consume excessive memory when the backend failed to start. Always-on host disk/RAM risk after a failed engine start.

4.94.0 all platforms: default logging driver for new Linux containers changed to local (automatic log rotation, lower disk use). endurance-coach compose already sets logging.driver: local with max-size 10m / max-file 3; media/*arr Compose that omit a logging driver will pick up the new default only for newly created containers.

4.94.0 Windows: WSL startup errors now explain when virtualization is disabled in firmware, nested virtualization is unavailable, or the Windows hypervisor is disabled at startup, with guidance for each condition.
4.94.0 all platforms: invalid JSON in a settings file now names the file that needs correcting instead of an unexpected error. Helpful if recovery/hardening scripts rewrite Docker config.

4.93.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop failed to start with an unexpected error when the engine needed more than five minutes to recover after an unclean shutdown. Directly relevant to this always-on host (configure_power_outage_hardening.ps1, post_boot_stack_recovery.ps1, restart_docker_desktop.ps1).

4.93.0 Windows: WSL integration proxy could fatally timeout at startup when restoring persisted bind mounts, especially with non-default wsl.conf [automount] root. Related to the 4.92.0 known issue that 4.94.0 now explicitly fixes. Review wsl.conf and media/*arr plus endurance-coach host bind mounts before upgrading.

4.93.0 Windows: a failed read of a WSL distro's config.json crashed the distro agent, disabled WSL integration, and prevented factory reset from cleaning ~/.docker. Can leave the engine/integration dead after a bad or partial distro config.

4.93.0 Windows: spurious 'WSL integration with distro unexpectedly stopped' dialogs fired while the engine was being stopped or restarted. Affects restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 stop-start cycles.

4.93.0 Windows: unhelpful error when WSL timed out registering the Docker Desktop Linux distribution; false 'Virtualization support not detected' when Virtual Machine Platform was enabled but vfpext was absent; WSL2 CLI credential store could reset to default on restart.

4.93.0 Windows: startup crash (exit code 151) when settings-store.json or daemon.json was saved with a UTF-8 BOM by an external editor or provisioning tool. enable_docker_autostart.ps1 uses Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 on those settings files (Windows PowerShell 5.x writes a BOM).

4.93.0 all platforms: file sharing directories (and other list settings) reverted to defaults after they were cleared and Docker Desktop restarted (desktop-feedback#515). VirtioFS / shared-folder settings for media/*arr bind mounts can silently reset.
4.93.0 security: VM-side code could request Unix socket port forwards, which could expose arbitrary host paths to manipulation. Also Engine v29.8.1. No named CVE id in the 4.93.0 notes.

4.93.0 Windows upgrade path: MSI installs never added the installing user to docker-users; update failures showed a generic error instead of installer details. This host's pin path is winget (update_docker_desktop.ps1), not MSI.

4.92.0 all platforms: published ports stayed unreachable for the life of the container when the host port was momentarily busy. Directly relevant to endurance-coach 5432/8000/8080 and media ports (Jellyfin 8096, Caddy 443, Sonarr 8989, Radarr 7878, Prowlarr 9696, Navidrome 4533, slskd 5030) during heal/restart races.

4.92.0 Windows: WSL 2 cross-distro bind-mount proxy could serve stale or incomplete directory contents for host paths on slow-to-mount drives (example: Storage Pool volumes). Applies to media/*arr bind mounts and endurance-coach host mounts (${USERPROFILE}/.garminconnect, ${USERPROFILE}/.endurance-coach).

4.92.0 Windows: Docker Desktop retried the WSL engine indefinitely without reporting an error when WSL could not load its own kernel modules; a misleading error claimed the WSL disk image had been deleted when WSL could not open it while registering the distribution.

4.92.0 Windows: Windows 10 hosts with inbox wsl.exe saw a raw error instead of the prompt to update WSL. Relevant if this host still uses inbox WSL (configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 also runs wsl --update).

4.92.0 Windows: single-file bind mounts on Docker VMM were broken; disk image location moves to a different drive always failed (desktop-feedback#548/#550). Relevant only if this host uses Docker VMM or relocates the disk image.
4.92.0 all platforms: Send Diagnostics hung or showed an unhelpful error when a proxy blocked the upload. Proxy-related; this host also uses ExpressVPN.

4.92.0 security: containerd updated to v2.3.5, addressing CVE-2026-53495. 4.94.0 further updates containerd to v2.3.6 (no additional CVE named). 4.96.0 bumps containerd again to v2.4.2 with no additional named CVE in the Desktop notes. 4.96.1 / 4.96.2 / 4.96.3 do not bump containerd further.

4.91.0 all platforms: a corrupt Docker network database, usually from an abrupt shutdown, prevented Docker Engine from starting and left a factory reset as the only recovery option. Directly relevant to this always-on host.

4.91.0 all platforms: Docker Compose rebuilt locally-built images on every Resource Saver wake (docker/desktop-feedback#507). endurance-coach compose uses build: . / image: endurance-coach:latest for api and mcp.

4.91.0 all platforms: the VM could shut down unexpectedly when idle timeout was set to 0; Docker Desktop sometimes took five extra minutes to report the engine as stopped when the VM stopped unexpectedly. Affects always-on idle/auto-pause and restart/unless-stopped recovery timing.
4.91.0 Windows: Docker Desktop stayed on Starting... indefinitely when WSL could not access the disk image location; it now reports the access failure with guidance instead of a generic WSL error.

4.90.0 Windows: startup hang on 'Starting' after a WinGet upgrade when install-settings.json has conflicting engine settings. Directly relevant to scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 (winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop).
4.90.0 / 4.89.0 Windows: Docker Desktop could fail to start after an ungraceful shutdown left a stuck socket. Relevant to power-loss recovery.
4.90.0 Windows: a failing third-party WSL plugin (example: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint WSL plugin) was reported as a missing Docker Desktop disk instead of naming the plugin that blocked WSL.

4.90.0 all platforms: bind-mount root intermittently reported ownership 0:0 (git 'detected dubious ownership'); repeatedly replacing files on a shared folder leaked VM disk space; VirtioFS renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) overwrote the target; mmap() of a Synchronized File Share file failed. Applies to endurance-coach host mounts and media/*arr bind mounts.
4.90.0 security: Kind cloud provider image v0.7.0 addresses CVE-2026-46595 and CVE-2026-39834. Low priority unless this host uses Kind / Docker Offload Kubernetes.

4.89.0 Resource Saver background container/image polling no longer wakes the engine. 4.88.0: HTTP 500 on startup/wake when the engine socket existed but was not yet listening; corrupted ~/.docker/daemon.json (null bytes after crash/power-loss) auto-recovers to defaults; docker ps port bindings include [::1]; Docker VMM inbound throughput regression (~0.3 GB/s) fixed.

4.87.0 Windows: Store-installed WSL repeatedly prompted for wsl --update (also used by configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1); misleading proxy errors named the destination instead of the unreachable upstream; Resource Saver / disk-limit UI fixes for Hyper-V and Docker VMM.

Pin 4.86.0 already includes unless-stopped / container-stop honoring on engine shutdown, VirtioFS AF_UNIX bidirectional sockets, OS-configured proxy Offload fix, and CVE-2026-17106 (docker container cp destination escape).
recommended_actions: Do not bump the Version default in scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 from this alert. Leave the pin at 4.86.0 until a human reviews 4.96.3 on this Windows host.
Do not change compose files, recovery scripts, or other stack config from this alert.

Treat 4.96.3 as the review target: continued eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust so an on-path attacker cannot intercept Docker CLI/daemon TLS (4.96.1/4.96.2 said this is batched; 4.96.3 is the next same-day component batch and does not repeat the upcoming-patches callout), plus remaining 4.96.2 Compose v5.6.1 and 4.96.1 Engine 29.9.2 / Buildx v0.38.1 / credential helpers v0.9.12. No named CVE id in 4.96.1, 4.96.2, or 4.96.3.

Because 4.96.1/4.96.2 said the CA fix is rolling out in batches, do not assume 4.96.3 finishes the eMudhra work just because this patch omitted the IMPORTANT callout. Still do not bump the pin from this alert.
Ignore the 4.96.3 Docker MCP v0.44.2, Init, Offload, Model Runner, Debug, and kubectl bumps for this stack. Coach mcp is the endurance-coach container, not Docker's MCP toolkit.

Before any upgrade, confirm no media/*arr or other Compose network uses 192.168.65.0/24 (Docker Desktop's internal range). An overlap can leave the engine stuck on Starting until the network is removed (4.96.0 / desktop-feedback#659).

Before any upgrade, confirm the Docker Desktop disk image / WSL data root is not under the installation directory (typically C:\Program Files\Docker). A 4.86.0-era path there can wipe engine disks (media volumes + postgres_data) on the way through 4.95.0. Also treat a busy/locked WSL data disk as a stop-ship until 4.96.0's mkfs-loop fix is understood.
Still treat 4.96.0 internal DHCP replies leaking onto the host LAN, engine-start hang on 192.168.65.0/24 overlap, and unusable WSL data disk triggering repeated mkfs attempts as in-delta.

Still treat 4.95.0 WSL data-disk deletion on update (desktop-feedback#667), Settings allowing that unsafe disk-image path, WinGet/update failure when app.asar is locked, and Hyper-V compact-after-restart as in-delta.

Still treat 4.94.0 WinGet/--always-run-service auto-start loss, the 4.92.0 WSL automount-timeout fix (desktop-feedback#695), Resource Saver pausing the VM before the Docker API is ready, and service-left-stopped-after-update as in-delta if upgrading from the 4.86.0 pin.

Before upgrading, check each WSL distro's /etc/wsl.conf for [automount] root=/ and avoid bind-mounting non-drive paths under /mnt (including /mnt/wslg). 4.94.0 explicitly fixes the 4.92.0 automount-timeout failure; 4.93.0 already had a related bind-mount proxy timeout fix.

If this host was installed with --always-run-service, plan to re-check the Docker Desktop service start mode after any WinGet upgrade (4.94.0 claims that auto-start is now preserved). Also confirm the engine is actually running after an update, not left stopped.

Still review remaining 4.93.0 items: unclean-shutdown start when engine recovery exceeds five minutes, WSL distro config.json crash that disabled integration, file-sharing list reset, Unix-socket port-forward host-path exposure, and UTF-8 BOM settings-store.json / daemon.json exit 151 (enable_docker_autostart.ps1 writes those files with Set-Content -Encoding UTF8).

Still review remaining 4.92.0 items if upgrading past the pin: published ports staying dead after a briefly busy host port, WSL2 bind-mount proxy serving stale/incomplete host dirs, WSL disk-image/kernel-module start hangs, containerd CVE-2026-53495.
Still review remaining 4.91.0 items: abrupt-shutdown network-DB recovery (was factory-reset-only), Compose rebuilds of endurance-coach on Resource Saver wake, idle-timeout 0 VM shutdown.

Before any upgrade, snapshot or inspect %APPDATA%\Docker\install-settings.json (and the all-users copy if present) so a WinGet hang on conflicting engine settings (still in 4.90.0) can be diagnosed. Do not save settings-store.json or daemon.json with a UTF-8 BOM (4.93.0 exit 151).

If upgrading later, run scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 only after a planned window; expect Docker restart plus heal_full_stack.ps1. Watch for TLS/registry failures from the eMudhra CA distrust landing in batches, LAN/VPN disruption from the pre-4.96.0 DHCP leak, engine-start hang on 192.168.65.0/24 overlap, WSL data-disk mkfs loops or deletion if the image path is under the install dir, app.asar lock during winget, the service not auto-starting after winget, Hyper-V compact/restart failure, 'Starting' hang, Resource Saver transient API errors on restart, engine recovery >5 min after unclean shutdown, published ports that never become reachable, stale media/*arr bind-mount listings, WSL integration dialogs during restarts, stuck-socket or corrupt-network-DB startup after power loss, and unexpected VM stop when idle timeout is 0.

After any upgrade, confirm image pulls and registry TLS still work (CLI/daemon CA distrust), Compose v5.6.1 did not change media/*arr or endurance-coach behavior, postgres/api/mcp (restart: unless-stopped) come back without a compose rebuild loop, published ports 5432/8000/8080 still bind, the WSL/engine disk is intact (not reformatted), file-sharing directories were not reset, the Docker Desktop service is set to automatic start, host LAN/VPN still routes as expected, and host bind-mount contents/ownership on ~/.garminconnect and ~/.endurance-coach are complete and not 0:0.

If WSL fails to start, check the real wsl.exe error (not a 'bad magic string'), disk-image path access (and that it is not under the install directory), whether the data disk is already in use before any format, WSL kernel-module load, automount / bind-mount proxy timeouts, distro config.json, firmware/nested virtualization / hypervisor-at-startup, vfpext/VMP, and named third-party WSL plugins (Defender) rather than a missing Docker disk. Kind CVEs can be ignored unless Kind/Offload Kubernetes is in use.
Use Automation Watchboard (yellow Update) as the cue to apply or skip 4.96.3 in Cursor.
